---
title: "Common settings"
---

This page collects the JupyterHub settings that matter most when you run Positron
Server for a group of users, such as a class, and explains what each one does.

Every setting on this page goes in `jupyterhub_config.py`, unless the text says
otherwise. Treat the values as starting points, then measure your own hardware and
number of users and adjust.

## Settings at a glance

| Setting | JupyterHub default | Starting point |
|---|---|---|
| `c.Spawner.pre_spawn_hook` | `None` | Sets `default_url` to `/positron/?tkn=<token>` with a new token for each session |
| `c.Spawner.mem_limit` | `None` | `4G` |
| `c.Spawner.cpu_limit` | `None` | `1` |

## Start students in Positron Server

A single-user server opens JupyterLab by default, and students reach Positron Server
from the launcher tile. `Spawner.default_url` changes where a session lands.

Positron Server validates a connection token on every HTTP and WebSocket request.
The token protects the port that Positron Server listens on, so only the student who
owns the session can connect to it. The launcher tile works because it carries that
token as a `tkn` query parameter. A bare `/positron` URL carries no token, so
Positron Server answers `403 Forbidden`.

To land students in Positron Server, make a new token when each session starts. Put
it in the session environment and in the landing URL:

```{.python filename="jupyterhub_config.py"}
import secrets

def positron_token_hook(spawner):
    token = secrets.token_hex(16)
    # Copy the dictionary. The configured value can be shared by every spawner.
    spawner.environment = {**spawner.environment, "POSITRON_CONNECTION_TOKEN": token}
    spawner.default_url = f"/positron/?tkn={token}"

c.Spawner.pre_spawn_hook = positron_token_hook
```

On TLJH, put this code in a file in `/opt/tljh/config/jupyterhub_config.d/`, then
run `sudo tljh-config reload`. The hook works with every spawner, and it keeps the
`PATH` that the [TLJH install script](deployment.qmd) sets.

Do not also set `c.Spawner.default_url = '/positron'`. If your configuration already
has a `pre_spawn_hook`, add these lines to that function. A second assignment
replaces the first hook.

The token changes each time a student's server starts, so a bookmarked Positron
Server URL stops working. Tell students to bookmark the JupyterHub address. The Hub
always sends them to the current session.

::: callout-important
Do not pin one token for all sessions through `POSITRON_CONNECTION_TOKEN`. Every
student sees the token in their own URL. On TLJH, all sessions run on the same host,
so a student who knows the token can connect to the Positron Server port of another
student and run code as that student.
:::

::: callout-note
Students still reach JupyterLab at `/user/<username>/lab` when they need the notebook
interface.
:::

## Cap memory and CPU per session

A Positron Server session uses more memory than an RStudio session or a plain Jupyter
kernel. The [memory requirements](configuration.qmd#memory-requirements) section
recommends at least 2.5 GB per session, and 4 GB for a standard workload.

```{.python filename="jupyterhub_config.py"}
c.Spawner.mem_limit = '4G'
c.Spawner.cpu_limit = 1
```

::: callout-important
`mem_limit` is a hard cap, not a share. A session that reaches the cap is killed, so
a value below the recommended allocation produces crashes during memory-intensive
work. The 2 GB floor suits a light workload only.
:::

::: callout-note
JupyterHub does not enforce these limits itself. The spawner has to implement them.
SystemdSpawner (used by TLJH) and DockerSpawner both do. LocalProcessSpawner does
not, and passes the values to the session as environment variables only.
:::

On The Littlest JupyterHub (TLJH), set the same limits through `tljh-config`:

```{.bash filename="Terminal"}
sudo tljh-config set limits.memory 4G
sudo tljh-config set limits.cpu 1
sudo tljh-config reload
```

## Lock Positron settings for a class

`POSITRON_ENFORCED_SETTINGS` locks settings so students cannot change them. Two
settings come up often for coursework:

```{.python filename="jupyterhub_config.py"}
c.Spawner.environment.update({
    "POSITRON_ENFORCED_SETTINGS": '{"ai.enabled":false,"extensions.autoUpdate":false}',
})
```

- **`ai.enabled`**: set to `false` to turn off every Positron AI feature at once. To
  turn features off one at a time, see the
  [Positron AI configuration reference](https://positron.posit.co/ai-configuration.html).
- **`extensions.autoUpdate`**: set to `false` to hold extension versions steady across
  a class for the length of a term.

For version requirements and the full behavior of locked settings, see the
[admin-enforced settings](configuration.qmd#admin-enforced-settings) section.

::: callout-important
Each assignment to `c.Spawner.environment` replaces the whole dictionary, so use
`.update()` to add a variable. The `PATH` from the [Get started](get_started.qmd)
guide then stays in place.

A setting on the spawner class takes precedence over `c.Spawner`. The TLJH install
script sets `c.SystemdSpawner.environment`, so on TLJH, JupyterHub ignores
`c.Spawner.environment`. Use `c.SystemdSpawner.environment.update(...)` instead, in a
file in `jupyterhub_config.d/` whose name sorts after `positron.py`, for example
`positron_enforced.py`.
:::
